Date of Notice: 2026-08-12
Requested Service: ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888
Treating Surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals & Grievances Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888), described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-12. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day deadline stated in that notice (due by 2027-02-08).

A note on policy citation: I requested, but as of the date of this letter have not yet received, the specific written clinical criteria, guideline title/number, and citation (including any MCG guideline reference) that Passport/Molina applied to reach this determination. Because I have not been given that document's actual text, I am not quoting or attributing any specific policy language to Passport/Molina in this letter. I am instead addressing the stated reason for denial — incomplete documentation — directly, by supplying the complete clinical record that supports medical necessity for this procedure, and I am formally renewing my request that Passport/Molina provide me and my surgeon with the specific criteria document(s), section(s), and effective date(s) used in this review, so that we may respond to them point by point if this appeal is not immediately approved.

Below is the clinical documentation that I understand was part of, or should have been part of, the prior authorization submission. If any of these records were missing from the original request, I ask that this appeal be considered together with this complete record set.

1. Diagnosis and imaging confirmation
   - MRI of the knee performed 2026-07-13 shows a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with an associated bone bruise pattern. The menisci are intact and there is no significant arthritis. This directly documents the structural injury for which ACL reconstruction is being requested.

2. Duration and course of symptoms
   - I have had 9 months of progressive knee pain that has not been relieved by rest, indicating this is not a transient or self-limited injury.

3. Completed, adequate trial of conservative (non-surgical) treatment
   - Supervised physical therapy for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, combined with bracing, over 14 weeks (2026-03-17 through 2026-06-23), with 16 visits completed, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
   - NSAID therapy for 8 months with inadequate relief.
   - A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-25, which provided only 2 weeks of partial relief.
   - Taken together, this represents a well-documented, multi-modality conservative treatment course that has failed to resolve my symptoms or restore function.

4. Objective findings of instability and exam findings
   - I continue to experience recurrent instability with pivoting motions and have had my knee give way twice on stairs, creating an ongoing fall/injury risk.
   - Physical examination shows positive provocative testing (e.g., findings consistent with ACL insufficiency) on the affected side, and range of motion is limited by pain.

5. Absence of contraindications
   - There is no active infection.
   - There is no untreated substance use.
   - My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.
   - There are no other documented factors that would make me a poor surgical candidate.

6. Surgeon's assessment
   - My treating orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has evaluated this complete clinical picture — confirmed complete ACL tear on MRI, failed conservative management, and functional instability — and has recommended ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888) as medically necessary.

In summary, the record contains: a confirmatory MRI, a 9-month symptom history, a completed and adequately dosed course of conservative therapy (physical therapy, bracing, NSAIDs, and injection) that failed to provide durable relief, objective exam findings of ligamentous instability, and functional impairment (recurrent giving-way) — without medical contraindications to surgery. I respectfully ask that Passport/Molina review this complete documentation, reverse the denial, and approve the requested ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888).

I also request the following, consistent with my appeal rights:
   - A copy of the specific clinical criteria/guideline (including title, policy or guideline number, and effective/reviewed date) that was applied to this request, so that I may verify what documentation standard was allegedly not met;
   - Confirmation of what specific piece(s) of documentation were considered "incomplete," since the enclosed record addresses diagnosis, duration, conservative treatment, imaging, exam findings, and absence of contraindications;
   - A copy of the complete case file, including any reviewer notes, used in the original determination;
   - Written confirmation of receipt of this appeal and the applicable review timeframe.

If it would assist in a faster resolution, I ask that Passport/Molina arrange a peer-to-peer conversation between its reviewing physician and Dr. Lindqvist to discuss the clinical basis for this request.

Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] if any additional information is needed. I can also be reached through the My Molina member portal.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Reese Iverson
Member ID: W871184265
